items.name: Coverage Verification
items.summary: Governs how quickly coverage determinations are made and communicated after a claim is assigned, ensuring policyholders receive a definitive coverage position early in the claim lifecycle and the carrier remains compliant with fair claims handling regulations.

subs.title: Coverage Confirmed Within 24 Hours of Assignment
subs.description: Upon assignment, the adjuster must review the policy in force, applicable endorsements, and loss facts to confirm whether coverage applies, completing the determination within 24 hours. Where coverage cannot yet be confirmed, the file must document the open questions and any reservation of rights consideration before the deadline passes.

subs.title: Denial Letters Within 72 Hours if No Coverage
subs.description: When the coverage review concludes that no coverage exists, a written denial letter citing the specific policy provisions relied upon must be issued to the insured within 72 hours. The letter must follow approved template language, reference state-specific notice requirements, and be retained in the claim file alongside the supporting coverage analysis.

items.name: Initial Contact
items.summary: Sets the expectation for prompt, documented outreach to the insured at the start of every claim, establishing early rapport, gathering loss facts while they are fresh, and creating an auditable record of the carrier's responsiveness.

subs.title: Insured Contacted Within 24 Hours of Assignment
subs.description: The assigned adjuster must make first contact with the insured within 24 hours of receiving the file, explaining the claims process, confirming loss details, and setting expectations for next steps. Contact by phone is preferred, with email or letter acceptable only after live contact attempts have failed.

subs.title: Contact Attempts Documented
subs.description: Every attempt to reach the insured, whether successful or not, must be recorded in the claim system with the date, time, channel used, and outcome. This record demonstrates good-faith handling in the event of a regulatory inquiry or bad-faith allegation and allows supervisors to verify the contact standard was met.

items.name: Intake SLA
items.summary: Defines the service-level commitments for the first hours of a reported loss, ensuring every new claim is promptly recognized and routed to a handling adjuster so that downstream investigation and contact standards can be met.

subs.title: FNOL Acknowledged Within 4 Hours
subs.description: Each first notice of loss, regardless of intake channel, must be acknowledged to the reporting party within 4 hours of receipt with a claim number and a description of what happens next. The acknowledgment timestamp is captured in the claim system and monitored against the SLA on intake dashboards.

subs.title: Assigned to Adjuster Within 24 Hours
subs.description: New claims must be triaged for line of business, severity, and complexity and assigned to an appropriately licensed and authorized adjuster within 24 hours of FNOL receipt. Assignments that cannot be completed in that window, such as catastrophe surge volumes, require supervisor notation explaining the delay and the interim handling plan.

items.name: Red Flag Indicators
items.summary: Establishes a structured fraud-detection discipline within claims handling so that suspicious loss characteristics are recognized consistently and routed to the Special Investigation Unit before settlement activity proceeds.

subs.title: Documented Red Flag Checklist
subs.description: Adjusters must apply a standardized red flag checklist covering indicators such as late reporting, prior claim history, inconsistent statements, and financial distress, and record the results in the claim file. The checklist is maintained by SIU, reviewed annually against emerging fraud schemes, and completion is a required step before significant payments are released.

subs.title: Referral to SIU Within 48 Hours if Triggered
subs.description: When checklist results or adjuster judgment indicate potential fraud, the claim must be referred to the Special Investigation Unit within 48 hours of the trigger being identified. The referral must summarize the indicators observed, and routine claim activity that could prejudice the investigation is paused pending SIU direction.

items.name: SIU Investigation Standards
items.summary: Governs the conduct of Special Investigation Unit cases from acceptance through resolution, ensuring investigations are planned, coordinated with authorities where appropriate, and measurable in their results.

subs.title: Investigation Plan Within 5 Days
subs.description: Within 5 days of accepting a referral, the SIU investigator must produce a written investigation plan identifying the suspected scheme, evidence to be gathered, interviews to be conducted, and target milestones. The plan is approved by the SIU manager and updated as the investigation develops.

subs.title: Law Enforcement Coordination Documented
subs.description: Any contact with law enforcement, state fraud bureaus, or the National Insurance Crime Bureau must be recorded in the SIU case file, including the agency, contact person, information shared, and statutory immunity provisions relied upon. Mandatory fraud reporting obligations in each jurisdiction must be satisfied and evidenced in the file.

subs.title: Outcome Tracked
subs.description: Each SIU case must be closed with a recorded disposition, such as fraud substantiated, unsubstantiated, claim withdrawn, or referred for prosecution, along with any savings or restitution attributed to the investigation. Aggregated outcomes feed SIU performance reporting and annual fraud plan filings where states require them.

items.name: Documentation Requirements
items.summary: Ensures the claim file is a complete, current, and self-supporting record of all handling activity, so that any reviewer, auditor, or successor adjuster can reconstruct the claim's history and the basis for every decision.

subs.title: All Claim Activity Documented in System Within 24 Hours
subs.description: Calls, inspections, coverage analyses, reserve rationale, and all other material claim activity must be entered into the claim system within 24 hours of occurring. Notes must be factual and professional, as the file may be produced in litigation or regulatory examination.

subs.title: Photos and Evidence Linked to File
subs.description: Photographs, estimates, police reports, recorded statements, and other evidentiary materials must be uploaded and attached to the correct claim file rather than held in email or local storage. Each item should be labeled with its source and date so the evidentiary chain remains intact through settlement, subrogation, or litigation.

items.name: Expert Engagement
items.summary: Independent adjusters, engineers, appraisers, and other outside experts may be retained only in accordance with the department's authority matrix, which defines who may approve the engagement, the approved vendor panels to draw from, and the expense thresholds requiring escalation. This keeps expert spend controlled and ensures specialists are used where claim complexity genuinely warrants them.

items.name: Investigation Standards
items.summary: Defines the core investigative steps and timeframes every claim must satisfy, so that liability, damages, and recovery opportunities are established on reliable evidence gathered while it is still available.

subs.title: Recorded Statements Within 14 Days
subs.description: Recorded statements from the insured, claimants, and material witnesses must be obtained within 14 days of assignment where a statement is warranted by the loss type or liability questions. Statements must follow approved question outlines, include the required consent language, and be transcribed or summarized into the claim file.

subs.title: Scene Inspection Within 72 Hours for Property
subs.description: For property losses, the damaged premises or scene must be inspected within 72 hours of assignment, either by the handling adjuster or an approved field resource. Prompt inspection preserves perishable evidence, supports accurate scoping of damages, and reduces the risk of disputes over pre-existing conditions.

subs.title: Subrogation Potential Identified
subs.description: During the initial investigation the adjuster must assess whether a third party may be legally responsible for the loss and flag the file for subrogation review when potential exists. Evidence supporting recovery, such as defective products or at-fault driver information, must be preserved and the statute of limitations noted.

items.name: Litigation Management
items.summary: Controls how litigated claims are defended and financially managed, ensuring counsel selection, case strategy, and reserving reflect the true legal exposure and keep defense costs proportionate to the matter.

subs.title: Defense Counsel From Approved Panel
subs.description: Defense of litigated claims must be assigned to firms on the carrier's approved panel, which is vetted for jurisdiction expertise, rate agreements, and adherence to billing and reporting guidelines. Use of non-panel counsel requires advance approval from the litigation manager with documented justification, such as a conflict or a specialty not represented on the panel.

subs.title: Litigation Plan Required
subs.description: Within the period set by counsel guidelines, defense counsel must submit a litigation plan covering liability assessment, damages evaluation, discovery strategy, motion practice, resolution strategy, and budget. The claims professional reviews and approves the plan and holds counsel to it at defined case milestones.

subs.title: Reserve Adjusted for Legal Exposure
subs.description: Once suit is filed or litigation becomes probable, the reserve must be reevaluated to reflect verdict potential, defense costs, and jurisdiction-specific factors rather than the pre-suit damages estimate alone. Reserve changes driven by litigation developments must be documented with counsel's evaluation as support.

items.name: Customer Satisfaction
items.summary: Establishes how the department measures and responds to the policyholder's experience of the claims process, treating claim service as a retention driver and ensuring dissatisfaction is surfaced and addressed quickly.

subs.title: Post-Claim Survey Sent
subs.description: A satisfaction survey must be issued to the insured after claim closure through the standard survey platform, covering responsiveness, communication clarity, and fairness of outcome. Response data is attributed to the handling adjuster and office for coaching and trend analysis.

subs.title: NPS Target Above 40
subs.description: The department maintains a Net Promoter Score target of greater than 40 across closed-claim surveys, monitored monthly by line of business. Scores trending below target trigger root-cause review of detractor feedback and corrective action plans owned by claims leadership.

subs.title: Complaints Escalated Within 24 Hours
subs.description: Customer complaints received through any channel, including department of insurance inquiries, must be escalated to the designated complaint handler within 24 hours of receipt. Each complaint is logged, investigated, and answered within regulatory timeframes, with outcomes fed back into quality reviews.

items.name: Cycle Time Targets
items.summary: Sets average claim duration benchmarks by claim type so the department can balance thorough investigation against the policyholder's interest in prompt resolution, with performance tracked from FNOL to closure on operational dashboards.

subs.title: Auto: 30 Days Average
subs.description: Auto physical damage and routine auto claims should resolve in an average of 30 days from FNOL to closure. Files open beyond the benchmark are flagged on aging reports for supervisor review of what is blocking resolution, such as parts delays or unresponsive parties.

subs.title: Property: 45 Days Average
subs.description: Property claims carry a 45-day average cycle time target, reflecting the additional time needed for inspection, scoping, and contractor estimates. Catastrophe-coded losses are measured separately so surge events do not distort the standard book's performance.

subs.title: Liability: 90 Days Average
subs.description: Liability claims are targeted to close within an average of 90 days, allowing for liability investigation, injury evaluation, and negotiation while discouraging files from drifting without active handling. Claims exceeding the average require a documented action plan toward resolution.

subs.title: Complex: 180 Days Average
subs.description: Claims designated complex, such as large losses, coverage disputes, or serious injury cases, are managed to a 180-day average. The extended target recognizes legitimate investigative and legal timelines while still requiring quarterly file strategy reviews to keep the claim progressing.

items.name: File Review Standards
items.summary: Defines the department's quality assurance program for claim files, providing a recurring, measurable check that handling standards are actually being followed and that reviewers apply those standards consistently.

subs.title: 10% of Files Reviewed Monthly
subs.description: Each month a sample equal to at least 10 percent of open and recently closed files per adjuster is selected for quality review against the department's audit criteria. Sampling must include a mix of claim types and severities, with targeted pulls added when prior reviews identified deficiencies.

subs.title: Quality Scorecard Maintained
subs.description: Review results are recorded on a standardized scorecard measuring dimensions such as coverage analysis, contact compliance, reserve accuracy, and documentation quality. Scores roll up to adjuster, team, and office levels and inform coaching plans, training priorities, and performance evaluations.

subs.title: Calibration Sessions Quarterly
subs.description: Quality reviewers and claims managers meet each quarter to score a common set of files and reconcile differences in interpretation of the audit criteria. Calibration outcomes are documented and the audit guide updated where the sessions reveal ambiguous standards.

items.name: Reinsurance Notification
items.summary: Governs the reporting of ceded claims to reinsurers so that contractual notice conditions are met, recoverables are protected, and the carrier preserves its right to reimbursement under both treaty and facultative placements.

subs.title: Treaty Notification Per Contract Terms
subs.description: Claims that meet or are likely to meet treaty attachment points, or that fall within categories the treaty designates as reportable regardless of size, must be noticed to the reinsurer within the timeframes and in the format the treaty specifies. The claims team coordinates with the ceded reinsurance function to confirm reporting thresholds for each program year and documents the notification in the claim file.

subs.title: Facultative Claims Reported Within 72 Hours
subs.description: Losses on policies with facultative reinsurance must be reported to the facultative reinsurer within 72 hours of the claim being identified as touching the certificate. Because facultative placements are policy-specific and often contain strict claims-cooperation clauses, late notice risks the recoverable, so the 72-hour internal standard deliberately runs ahead of most certificate requirements.

items.name: Initial Reserve Standards
items.summary: Establishes the discipline for setting the first case reserve on every claim, ensuring the carrier's booked liabilities reflect a reasoned estimate of ultimate exposure from the earliest days of the file.

subs.title: Initial Reserve Set Within 72 Hours Based on Reserve Worksheet
subs.description: The handling adjuster must establish an initial case reserve within 72 hours of assignment using the standard reserve worksheet, which walks through indemnity components, expected expenses, and applicable deductibles or limits. Placeholder or formula-only reserves are acceptable solely as a system default pending the worksheet-based evaluation.

subs.title: Documented Rationale Required
subs.description: The basis for the initial reserve, including damages assumptions, liability assessment, and any comparable claim references, must be recorded in the claim file alongside the worksheet. This rationale gives subsequent reserve reviews a baseline and supports actuarial and audit reliance on case reserve data.

items.name: Large Loss Threshold
items.summary: Defines the financial severity tiers at which claims must move to more experienced handlers and management oversight, ensuring the carrier's largest exposures receive expertise and supervision proportional to their potential impact.

subs.title: Claims Over $100K Require Senior Adjuster Assignment
subs.description: Any claim with incurred value or realistic exposure exceeding $100,000 must be assigned or reassigned to a senior adjuster with the experience and authority appropriate to large losses. The reassignment is made promptly once the threshold is recognized, with a documented file transfer summarizing status and open actions.

subs.title: Over $500K Requires Manager Oversight
subs.description: Claims exceeding $500,000 in incurred value or exposure are placed under active manager oversight, including participation in reserve and settlement decisions and periodic strategy reviews documented in the file. These claims also feed the large loss report distributed to claims leadership, actuarial, and ceded reinsurance.

items.name: Reserve Adequacy Review
items.summary: Requires structured reassessment of case reserves as claims develop, keeping booked amounts aligned with current facts and ensuring material reserve movements receive management scrutiny.

subs.title: Reserves Reviewed at 30, 60, and 90 Days
subs.description: Open claims must undergo a documented reserve adequacy review at the 30, 60, and 90 day marks, with the adjuster confirming the reserve still reflects known damages, liability posture, and expense expectations. Each review note must either affirm the current reserve with reasoning or record the adjustment made.

subs.title: Manager Approval for Changes Over $25K
subs.description: Any single reserve change exceeding $25,000, upward or downward, requires manager review and approval before posting. The approval captures the development driving the change and guards against both stair-stepped under-reserving and unexplained reserve takedowns.

items.name: Payment Processing
items.summary: Governs the issuance of claim payments after settlement, ensuring funds reach the correct parties quickly while protecting the carrier against misdirected or fraudulent disbursements.

subs.title: Payments Issued Within 5 Business Days of Settlement Agreement
subs.description: Once a settlement is agreed and all payment conditions are satisfied, the indemnity payment must be issued within 5 business days. Prompt payment supports state prompt-pay statutes and customer satisfaction commitments, and aging of approved-but-unpaid settlements is monitored on operations reports.

subs.title: Proper Payee Verification
subs.description: Before release, the adjuster must verify the payee's identity and entitlement, including correct legal names, lienholder and mortgagee interests, attorney representation, and any required multi-party endorsements. Bank detail changes or unusual payment instructions must be independently confirmed to guard against payment redirection fraud.

items.name: Release Documentation
items.summary: Ensures every settlement is legally final and that the carrier's recovery rights survive the closing of the claim, by tying payment to properly executed release documents.

subs.title: Signed Release Required Before Payment
subs.description: Settlement payments to claimants may not be issued until a release appropriate to the claim type and jurisdiction has been signed and returned. The release must use approved template language, identify all released parties and claims, and be reviewed for alterations before payment is authorized.

subs.title: Subrogation Rights Preserved Where Applicable
subs.description: Release and settlement documents must be drafted so they do not extinguish the carrier's subrogation or contribution rights against responsible third parties. Where recovery potential exists, the file must confirm that the executed release language protects those rights before the claim is closed.

items.name: Settlement Authority
items.summary: Defines the financial authority framework under which claims are resolved, ensuring settlement decisions are made at the appropriate level and reflect the merits of each claim rather than expediency.

subs.title: Adjuster Authority Per Level
subs.description: Each adjuster holds documented settlement authority tied to their grade, license status, and demonstrated performance, and may not commit the carrier beyond that limit. Settlements above an individual's authority must be escalated for approval before any offer is extended, and authority grants are reviewed annually.

subs.title: Manager Approval for Policy Limits Settlements
subs.description: Any settlement at or near policy limits requires manager approval before the offer is made or accepted, given the bad-faith exposure attached to limits demands. The approval must be documented with the manager's evaluation of liability, damages, and the timing of the demand.

subs.title: No Nuisance Payments
subs.description: Claims without supporting liability or damages may not be settled simply to avoid handling or defense costs. Every payment must be justified by the documented merits of the claim, preserving the integrity of loss data and avoiding signaling that meritless claims will be paid.

items.name: Recovery Standards
items.summary: Establishes the department's discipline for pursuing recoveries from responsible third parties, turning subrogation from an afterthought into a measured contributor to loss results.

subs.title: Subrogation Potential Evaluated on Every Claim
subs.description: A subrogation assessment is a mandatory step on every claim, with the adjuster recording whether recovery potential exists and the basis for that conclusion. Files with potential are referred to the subrogation unit with the supporting evidence preserved, and a no-potential determination must be affirmatively documented rather than left blank.

subs.title: Recovery Tracked to Closure
subs.description: Each referred subrogation matter must be tracked from demand through negotiation, arbitration, or litigation until funds are collected or the pursuit is formally closed with a documented reason. Recoveries are recorded against the originating claim so net loss figures and deductible reimbursements to insureds are accurate.

subs.title: Contingency Fee Approval
subs.description: Engaging outside recovery vendors or counsel on a contingency fee basis requires advance approval at the designated authority level, with the fee percentage and case-selection criteria documented. Approved arrangements are monitored for net recovery performance to confirm contingency placement outperforms in-house pursuit for the referred inventory.
